outputs.summary:
**Reported bug, confirmed by the person:** an epic with unsaved draft changes reopened on its saved plan ("REV n · SAVED", the draft hidden behind View draft) after visiting another epic, so after saving one epic every other epic looked "out of draft".

**Root cause:** `src/renderer/src/epic/workspaceState.ts`. `initialWorkspaceState()` started every mount at `view: 'saved'`, and `resolveView` (called from `loadSucceeded`) kept `'saved'` whenever a saved revision existed. `EpicWorkspace` remounts per folder and epic, so the view the person left was forgotten on every visit.

**Fix (renderer only):** the first load picks the view: the person's remembered choice for that epic, else Draft when the draft differs from the saved plan (`draftChanged`), else Saved. Later loads keep the view on screen, so background refreshes never flip it. Explicit switches (Edit draft, View draft, View saved) are remembered per folder and epic for the app session in an in-memory store (`epic/viewMemory.ts`, provided through React context). Save and Discard show Saved and forget the choice, so the next draft opens by the default rule.

Kept from attempt 1 (already merged): `draftChanged` on epic summaries, the sidebar badge only for real changes, and the two-folder isolation tests in `src/integration/epicDrafts.test.ts`.

**Root cause:** report entries are free text such as "DM-1 Confirm epic is visible in the app: verified via list_epics; …". `resolveRow` in `checkpoint/gateView.ts` only recognised an entry that was exactly a ticket id or key, so every sentence went into `ReportRow.key` with an empty title, and `Rows` in `CheckpointScreen.tsx` rendered it in `.cp-key`, the fixed 72 px first track of `.cp-row` (`grid-template-columns: 72px minmax(0, 1fr) auto`). A second squeeze in the checks list (name and detail shrinking side by side) is fixed by letting the row wrap so the detail drops under the name. followUps.title: Kill the two surviving EpicWorkspace.tsx mutants

risks: Screenshots come from an isolated dev build against throwaway copies of the repository records, not the installed app (v0.8.0). The installed app shows none of this until a release is built from main.
mechanicus-ui-revamp is not pushed or merged. It also carries the untracked .darkmechanicus epic records and .mcp.json in the working tree, which were never committed.
The primary-vs-danger comparison screenshot in DM-7 is staged: the harness added a danger button beside "New epic", since no screen shows both.
theme.contrast.test.ts ties :root to the palette doc in both directions, so any future token change must update docs/design/palette.md section 3 (and section 5 for contrast pairs).
fireguard grades every module changed against main, so each worker re-graded the whole epic (50 to 75 minutes per run), and its mutation gate rewrites source files in place.
content.summary: Sprint 2 met its goal: the whole app now uses the Mechanicus palette and the tech-priest greets new users. DM-6 applied the approved palette to the `:root` tokens behind a contrast guard test that also keeps the tokens and `docs/design/palette.md` in step. DM-7 moved primary actions, focus rings and the active sidebar row to crimson with bone titles, and DM-8 did the same for the epic workspace, graph, ticket panel and checkpoint, including a lens-green running glow and token-driven edge arrowheads. DM-9 put the mascot on the welcome and onboarding screens. DM-10 integrated the branch, re-ran every check, took the final screenshots and rewrote the design README. All five tickets were accepted on their first attempt, and every epic success criterion (s1 to s8) has evidence. Merging `mechanicus-ui-revamp` into `main` is a separate step for the person.
